Key Activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Develops new methods and techniques based on leading edge international developments, to meet the needs of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Assesses the implications of new approaches and makes recommendations for their adoption.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on the critical programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert recommendations, analysis and advice to senior managers in government (from various divisions within Statistics Canada and in key client departments such as Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada) and officials in industry (data providers and users), academia, other national and international statistical institutions and special interest groups.

Oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes within the highly specialized realm of temporal and spatial consumer prices indexes. Determines departmental and government-wide impacts and implications and makes recommendations for change.
Implements new systems or methodologies and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates their cost, efficiency and productivity
Supervision of project teams responsible for statistical outputs, research projects or studies and management of the financial resources attached to each project.

Work is done within the context of temporal and spatial indexes which are used throughout Statistics Canada (i.e., Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts), throughout government and industry to index payments worth billions of dollars, and by the Bank of Canada, as the basis for the country’s inflation targeting and monetary policy. Impact of errors is extremely high and cuts across Statistics Canada, other departments and throughout the economy. These factors add to the priority, complexity and scrutiny of the work of this position.

Decision Making: Reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs. Recommendations based on this work have the ability to influence the direction of major corporate initiatives, programs and policies, including those related to big data (e.g., scanner data, web-scraped data).

Initiates changes and implements new systems or methodologies and processes, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software, and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits. Recommendations lead to changes in approach for the program and take into consideration risks and impacts related to the changes and the use of the resulting program data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Manages complex studies related to the temporal and spatial consumer prices program, determines the objectives, content and methodology of such work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact other statistical programs such as Producer Prices and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts.

Determines objectives and priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and innovative solutions and recommendations to senior management on course of action and outcomes, or on significant issues affecting temporal and spatial price index programs.
Leadership And Operational Management: Provides advanced subject matter expertise within a multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project team environment to facilitate big data or temporal and spatial consumer price index research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals.

Assesses and recommends human and financial resource needs to achieve research and project objectives. Monitors the scope, schedule and cost of the work against approved baselines. Provides input into ongoing and strategic financial planning exercises.

Manages multi-disciplinary intradepartmental and/or interdepartmental project teams involved in research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term project goals.
For project team members, establishes work objectives and training related to project requirements, monitors achievements and provides input into performance evaluations.
Communication: Provides expert advice and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national agencies and academics on the results of research and analytical studies, economic and socio-economic theories and principles and statistical concepts and methods as they relate to temporal and spatial consumer price indices.

Attends divisional and intradepartmental meetings and represents the division in interdepartmental and international meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in the field of temporal and spatial consumer price indices or big data. Represents, expresses and defends the viewpoint, priorities, conceptual integrity and the validity of methods of the program in venues where decisions are made in order to promote the organization’s interests and influence conceptual directions.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data and conceptual frameworks, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of the concepts, statistical and analytical approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in layman’s terms in order to maintain the department's reputation for producing high quality data.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of economic and sociological principles, concepts and theories, especially as they relate to price index number theory, and specific knowledge of temporal and spatial consumer price indexes. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC. It is also required to provide expert evaluation of impacts and risks associated with proposed program changes on the use of the resulting program data for other Statistics Canada programs such as the Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, as well as for government-wide and economy-wide uses such as indexation and monetary policy uses.

Expert knowledge of systems, systems design and practices relevant for the maintenance and development of the temporal and spatial price index statistical programs. *related to the development environment only

Expert knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of temporal and spatial price index data in order to develop new methods and techniques and provide expert advice to internal and external stakeholders.
Advanced knowledge of resource and project management practices and principles in order to manage project teams and deliver on high priority projects related to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Advanced knowledge of the methodologies related to the highly specialized fields, such as big data in order to performed detailed analysis and assess new methods relevant to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods is required to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data within the context of temporal and spatial price index programs and to provide technical advice to other professionals.
Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of international frameworks (Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, Prices, etc.), their conceptual building blocks and their interdependencies to contribute in a meaningful way to the evaluation and impact assessment of concepts and compilation methods within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of divisional mandate, policies, priorities, practices, standards and procedures as well as existing databases and conceptual frameworks applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical and development projects and to determine or recommend changes.

Knowledge of STC mandate, policies, priorities, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and in the elaboration of recommendations for change to the program.

Knowledge of current and emerging economic issues in Canada and internationally as they relate to temporal and spatial price indexes, to understand needs for new data, analyze the data and assess their impact on the work of Consumer Prices Division and share expertise internally and/or with international organizations.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent legislation such as the Foreign Service Directives, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments (e.g., Bank of Canada, Finance Canada, Treasury Board Secretariat), agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent, and to apply within the context of establishing big data applications for use in the temporal and spatial price index programs.

Knowledge of the uses of temporal and spatial indexes within the mandates and legislation of other federal organizations such as the Bank of Canada, Finance Canada and Treasury Board Secretariat. This knowledge is important so that proposed changes to the temporal and spatial index programs can be assessed to ensure that outputs continue to meet the legislated requirements and mandates of stakeholders without negative impacts on those uses.
Research and analysis: Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of price index data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Investigates and challenges existing conceptual frameworks from multiple disciplines and examines multiple variables from distinct sources within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes to reach new conclusions or generate new solutions. Researches cutting-edge applications of new data sources, including those related to big data to make recommendations on changes to the program. Recommendations made result from work which is evaluated through the lenses of conceptual integrity, operational viability and a deep understanding of the needs of key users for applying the data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data. Continuously researches and evaluates new data sources in order to maintain the program's relevance and accuracy.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevance in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and economic conditions. It is necessary to understand and interpret present policy issues and the economic conditions of Canadians.
